statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across Hippo pathway genes, the study identified 85 loss-of-function missense mutations and worked out the mechanisms behind them.
statements.evidence: We identify a total of 85 loss-of-function (LOF) missense mutations for Hippo pathway genes and elucidate their underlying mechanisms.
statements.note: The abstract gives the count of 85 LOF missense mutations and states that their mechanisms were elucidated.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Pharmacological inhibition of JNK suppressed the growth of tumors carrying NF2 loss-of-function mutations.
statements.evidence: but also gain an oncogenic role for NF2 by activating the VANGL-JNK pathway
statements.note: The abstract reports that the NF2 mutants activate VANGL-JNK signaling but describes no experiment blocking JNK or any treatment effect on tumor growth.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Loss-of-function mutations in the zinc-finger domain of MOB1, found in head and neck cancer, enhance tumor growth.
statements.evidence: we reveal zinc-finger domain as an integral structure for MOB1 function, whose LOF mutations in head and neck cancer promote tumor growth
statements.note: The abstract identifies the zinc-finger domain as essential for MOB1 and says its LOF mutations in head and neck cancer promote tumor growth.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: NF2 loss-of-function mutations derived from schwannoma and meningioma both abolish NF2's tumor-suppressive activity and confer an oncogenic function via VANGL-JNK signaling.
statements.evidence: the schwannoma/meningioma-derived NF2 LOF mutations not only inhibit its tumor suppressive function in the Hippo pathway, but also gain an oncogenic role for NF2 by activating the VANGL-JNK pathway
statements.note: The abstract states both effects of these NF2 mutations: loss of tumor suppression and a gained oncogenic role through VANGL-JNK activation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: At cis-eQTLs of genes linked to spikelet number per panicle, alleles were under positive selection, with those raising SPP strongly favored.
statements.evidence: alleles at cis-expression quantitative trait loci of SPP-associated genes underwent positive selection, with a strong preference for alleles increasing SPP
statements.note: The abstract reports positive selection at these cis-eQTLs with a strong preference for SPP-increasing alleles.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The integrative cis/trans method pinpointed 36 putative causal genes for spikelet per panicle, among them SDT (MIR156j) and OsMADS17.
statements.evidence: We identified 36 putative causal genes of SPP, including SDT (MIR156j) and OsMADS17
statements.note: The abstract gives the count of 36 putative causal SPP genes and names SDT (MIR156j) and OsMADS17 among them.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Experiments confirmed the inferred regulation of SDT expression by OsMADS17.
statements.evidence: inferred that OsMADS17 regulates SDT expression, which was experimentally validated
statements.note: The abstract says the inferred OsMADS17-to-SDT regulatory link was experimentally validated.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Overexpressing OsMADS17 in rice plants increased grain yield.
statements.evidence: inferred that OsMADS17 regulates SDT expression, which was experimentally validated
statements.note: The abstract validates only that OsMADS17 regulates SDT expression; it reports no overexpression experiment and no yield measurement for any gene.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Giant virus abundance in Lake Mendota rose after the invasive predatory zooplankton arrived in 2009.
statements.evidence: A co-occurrence network analysis indicates increased virus-host interactions following the introduction of an invasive predatory zooplankton in 2009
statements.note: The abstract reports more inferred virus-host interactions in a co-occurrence network after the invasion, not a change in giant virus abundance, which it never quantifies.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Genome-wide substitution rates of the giant viruses were comparable to those of co-occurring bacteria yet markedly slower than those of smaller dsDNA phages.
statements.evidence: giant viruses exhibit genome-wide substitution rates similar to co-occurring bacteria but significantly slower than smaller dsDNA phages
statements.note: The abstract makes exactly this two-way comparison of substitution rates: similar to bacteria, significantly slower than small dsDNA phages.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Horizontal gene transfer affected a larger fraction of giant virus genes (29%) than gene duplication did (23%).
statements.evidence: gene duplication (23% of genes) and horizontal gene transfer (29% of genes) as key drivers of genomic innovation
statements.note: The abstract gives 23% of genes for duplication and 29% for horizontal transfer, so transfer covers the larger share.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: After the 2009 zooplankton invasion, the number of positively selected viral genes increased significantly, especially genes involved in infection.
statements.evidence: there is a significant increase in positively selected genes post-invasion, particularly those related to infection
statements.note: The abstract reports a significant post-invasion rise in positively selected genes, with infection-related genes singled out.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: POLD4 is among the genes whose structural variants and CpG island methylation were associated with patient survival.
statements.evidence: Genes with SVs and CGI methylation associated with patient survival include POLD4.
statements.note: The abstract names POLD4 as a gene with SVs and CGI methylation linked to patient survival.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: For thousands of CpG island or enhancer methylation probes, both rare and common nearby SV breakpoints were linked to differential tumor methylation across histologic types.
statements.evidence: For thousands of methylation probes for CpG Islands (CGIs) or enhancers, rare and common SV breakpoints upstream or downstream associate with differential methylation in tumors spanning various histologic types
statements.note: The abstract reports associations for thousands of CGI or enhancer probes, involving both rare and common SV breakpoints, across tumor histologies.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: SV-associated methylation differences were more frequent in high-grade gliomas than in other pediatric brain tumor types.
statements.evidence: rare and common SV breakpoints upstream or downstream associate with differential methylation in tumors spanning various histologic types
statements.note: The abstract says the associations span various histologic types but makes no comparison between tumor types and does not single out high-grade glioma.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: SV breakpoints lying inside CpG islands or within H3K36me3 or H3K9me3 histone marks were associated with altered CGI methylation.
statements.evidence: SV breakpoints falling within CGIs or histone marks H3K36me3 or H3K9me3 associate with differential CGI methylation.
statements.note: The abstract states that breakpoints within CGIs or these two histone marks associate with differential CGI methylation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Tracking ctDNA fragmentation signal longitudinally within individual patients made early cancer detection possible.
statements.evidence: intra-patient longitudinal analysis of ctDNA fragmentation signal enabled early cancer detection
statements.note: The abstract states that intra-patient longitudinal analysis of the fragmentation signal enabled early cancer detection.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A machine learning classifier separated TP53-mutant from TP53-wildtype cfDNA samples with AUC-ROC values ranging from 0.710 to 1.000.
statements.evidence: Machine learning classification resulted in robust differentiation between TP53 mutant versus wildtype cfDNA samples (AUC-ROC = 0.710-1.000)
statements.note: The abstract reports the AUC-ROC range 0.710-1.000 for distinguishing TP53 mutant from wildtype cfDNA samples.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with healthy TP53-wildtype controls, LFS individuals had a higher proportion of A/T nucleotides at cfDNA fragment ends.
statements.evidence: LFS individuals exhibit an increased prevalence of A/T nucleotides at fragment ends
statements.note: The abstract reports an increased prevalence of A/T nucleotides at fragment ends in LFS individuals, the comparison group being the healthy TP53-wildtype controls.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The A/T-rich fragment ends in LFS carriers arise from altered nuclease activity caused by the TP53 mutation.
statements.evidence: We find that LFS individuals exhibit an increased prevalence of A/T nucleotides at fragment ends, dysregulated nucleosome positioning at p53 binding sites
statements.note: The abstract describes the end-nucleotide difference but proposes no enzymatic or molecular cause for it, so a nuclease mechanism is neither stated nor ruled out.
